structured.business_case: Across our three hospital sites, 23% of supplier invoices were paid after their 30-day terms from January to June 2026. Late payments to our suppliers are costing us: we paid about £62,000 in late-payment interest and lost early-payment discounts last year, and three key medical suppliers put us on stop twice this year, which held up ward stock.

structured.voc_summary: Our customers are the suppliers, who need paying on the agreed 30-day terms, and our own ward managers, who need stock to keep arriving. Suppliers complain most about payments arriving late and not knowing when they will be paid; ward managers about deliveries being held. One more thing: suppliers also told us they cannot see the status of an invoice once it is submitted.

critical_to_quality.need: payments made on the agreed 30-day terms
critical_to_quality.requirement: paid within 30 days of the invoice date on every invoice
no supplier puts us on stop in a quarter

structured.problem_statement: From January to June 2026, 23% of supplier invoices processed by the accounts payable team across our three hospital sites were paid after their 30-day terms. Suppliers chase us by phone and email, and some put us on stop, which delays ward stock and costs interest, lost discounts, and supplier trust. The delays occur at the resolve mismatches and approve steps, where invoices wait.

problem_5w2h.why: interest, lost discounts and supplier stops

baseline_estimate.raw: One metric: late payment rate, in %, meaning the share of supplier invoices paid more than 30 days after the invoice date. It is about 23% today, from the AP ledger for January to June 2026. It feeds our finance KPI, creditor days.

target_value.raw: Late payment rate: under 5% of supplier invoices.

project_scope.in_scope: Invoice receipt to payment release for purchase-order invoices at our three hospital sites
project_scope.out_scope: Non-PO invoices, payroll, procurement tendering, and the ERP system itself

structured.goal_statement: Reduce the late payment rate from 23% to under 5% by 31 March 2027, and keep it under 5% for three months after that.

target_value.raw: Late payment rate: under 5% of supplier invoices.

structured.target_date: We plan to finish the project by 31 March 2027 (2027-03-31).

benefits_analysis.cost_of_gap: About £68,000 a year in interest and lost discounts, from the savings calculation.
benefits_analysis.realisation_schedule: Starting in Q2 2027 at about £17,000 a quarter.
benefits_analysis.finance_contact: Sam Reid, management accountant, who will validate the figure.

result.calculation_note: (23% baseline − 5% target) × 42000 units/year × 9 per unit = 68040 a year. Check the units agree: the rates are shares of the yearly volume, and the unit cost is the cost of one defect.

structured.secondary_metrics: Two things must not get worse: the number of supplier payment queries the AP team handles each month, and AP staff overtime hours. Both should stay at or below today's levels.

problems.note: Approvers on leave and nobody covers

structured.issues_and_barriers: Two barriers: the three sites use different approval routes, and an ERP change freeze until January limits system changes. One risk: AP staff turnover over the winter.
